english: Where does this road lead?
tip: куда (kuda = where to) asks about direction and pairs with motion verbs like ведёт (vedyot = leads).

english: Dad bought a new car.
tip: купил (kupil) is perfective, a finished one-time buy; imperfective покупал (pakupal) would mean was buying or used to buy.

english: What a beautiful building!
tip: какое (kakoe = what a) is neuter, matching здание (zdanie = building). красивое (krasivaye) agrees in neuter too; a masculine noun would take какой (kakoy).

english: The nurse runs every morning.
tip: бегает (begaet = runs) is the habitual form for repeated action, fitting каждое утро (kazhdaye utra = every morning). One run in progress would be бежит (bezhit).

english: I am thirty-two years old.
tip: два (dva = two) takes genitive singular: два года (dva goda = two years), not the plural годы (gody). Numbers 2, 3, 4 all do this.

english: She is twenty-one years old.
tip: один (adin = one) keeps the noun nominative singular: двадцать один год (dvadtsat adin god = twenty-one years), not года (goda). Numbers ending in 1 usually do this.

english: How long is the trip?
tip: сколько (skolka = how much) takes genitive: сколько времени (skolka vremeni = how much time). The base время (vremya) shifts to времени.

english: The doctor usually listens to music.
tip: музыку (muzyku = music) is the object form of музыка (muzyka). Most feminine nouns change their ending when they are the direct object.

english: Until tomorrow, have a good evening.
tip: хорошего вечера (kharosheva vechera = good evening) uses genitive: good wishes are stated in the genitive, literally 'of a good evening', not nominative.

english: What is your shoe size?
tip: размер обуви (razmer obuvi = shoe size): the second noun goes genitive to mean 'size of footwear'. Base обувь (obuv) becomes обуви.

english: What happened to your car?
tip: с (s = with) takes instrumental: с твоей машиной (s tvayey mashinay = with your car). Base машина (mashina) becomes машиной.

english: Whose umbrella is this on the table?
tip: чей (chey = whose) is masculine to match зонтик (zontik = umbrella). A feminine noun would take чья (chya) instead.

english: He works even if he is sick.
tip: даже если (dazhe esli = even if) introduces a concession: даже если болеет (baleyet = is sick), he still works.

target: У каждого человека есть свои мечты.
english: Every person has their own dreams.
tip: свои (svoi = one's own) points back to the subject and matches the thing owned: свои мечты (svoi mechty = one's own dreams).

target: Мне тридцать два года, я инженер.
english: I am thirty-two years old, I'm an engineer.
tip: мне (mne = to me) is dative: age is stated with dative, literally 'to me thirty-two years', not with я (ya = I).

target: Добрый день, могу я вам чем-нибудь помочь?
english: Good afternoon, can I help you with something?
tip: помочь (pamoch = to help) takes dative with no word for 'to': помочь вам (pamoch vam = help you). вам is the dative of вы (vy = you).

english: She can't swim.
tip: умеет (umeet) means know how to, a learned skill, not passing ability. не умеет плавать (ne umeet plavat) = never learned to swim.

english: The homework was difficult.
tip: Neuter subjects take было in the past: задание было (zadanie bylo = the assignment was); masculine был (byl), feminine была (byla).

english: He is twenty-five years old.
tip: Russian gives age with the person in the dative, not the nominative; ему (yemu = to him) is that dative, meaning he is the one who is twenty-five.

english: I don't like this movie.
tip: нравится (nravitsya = is pleasing) puts the liker in the dative; мне (mne = to me) is that dative, so the line reads the movie does not please me.

english: He doesn't work on weekends.
tip: по (po) plus the dative marks a repeated occasion. по выходным (po vykhadnym) = on weekends, meaning every weekend, not a single one.

target: У меня нет времени на это.
english: I don't have time for this.
tip: нет (net = there is no) forces the genitive on the missing thing. нет времени (net vremeni = no time) uses the genitive, not the nominative.

target: Тебе не стоит волноваться из-за экзамена.
english: You shouldn't worry about the exam.
tip: стоит (stoit = is worth) with a dative person gives soft advice; тебе (tebe = to you) не стоит (ne stoit) means you would be better off not doing it.

english: The farmer picks apples in autumn.
tip: Seasons take the instrumental to mean in that season. осенью (osen'yu = in autumn) needs no preposition, the ending alone carries in.

english: The kitchen smells of fresh baking.
tip: пахнет (pakhnet = smells) takes the instrumental for the scent. свежей выпечкой (svezhey vypechkay) = of fresh baking, with no separate word for of.

english: There are twenty-five students in the class.
tip: Numbers five and above usually take a genitive plural noun. пять учеников (pyat uchenikov = students) uses the genitive plural, not the plain plural.

target: Мы никогда не были в Париже.
english: We have never been to Paris.
tip: Negation stacks in Russian: никогда (nikagda = never) still needs не (ne) before the verb, никогда не были (nikagda ne byli = have never been).

target: Не могли бы вы закрыть окно?
english: Would you mind closing the window?
tip: могли бы (magli by) is the polite could you. The particle бы (by) is what softens a request into would you mind.

target: Здравствуйте, меня зовут Иван, очень приятно познакомиться.
english: Hello, my name is Ivan, very nice to meet you.
tip: меня зовут (menya zavut = me they call) is the standard way to give your name. меня (menya) is the object, so there is no word for I.

target: Я приехал из Москвы две недели назад.
english: I arrived from Moscow two weeks ago.
tip: назад (nazad = ago) comes after the time span: две недели назад (dve nedeli nazad = two weeks ago), never before it.
